name: orb_multi_stock_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Individual stock ORB breakouts have ~52% win rate, but a portfolio approach — trading ORB breakouts across 5-8 uncorrelated stocks simultaneously — improves the daily portfolio win rate to ~70%+ through diversification. When multiple stocks break their ORBs in the same direction on the same morning, it signals broad institutional flow that reinforces each individual signal. The portfolio approach also reduces variance: individual stock ORB can have ±100bps daily swings, but the 5-8 stock portfolio has ±30-40bps, making the strategy more consistent. The inefficiency exists because most retail traders only have bandwidth to monitor 1-2 ORB setups, missing the portfolio diversification benefit.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents on NSE, sorted by ORB signal quality
stock_filter: top 5-8 stocks by today's ORB signal strength (volume confirmation + gap alignment + VIX filter); all must have volume > ₹100cr/day
indicators: ORB_high_15[i] = highest(high[i], bars 09:15 to 09:30) for each stock i
ORB_low_15[i] = lowest(low[i], bars 09:15 to 09:30) for each stock i
portfolio_correlation = avg pairwise correlation of selected stocks
ATR_14[i] = ATR(high, low, close, 14) per stock

conditions: at least 3 stocks have ORB breakout signals (portfolio threshold)
long.confirmation: each stock's breakout confirmed with 2 consecutive closes above ORB_high

conditions: at least 3 stocks have ORB breakdown signals
short.confirmation: each stock's breakdown confirmed with 2 consecutive closes below ORB_low

entry.entry_price: market orders across all selected stocks simultaneously

exit.target: per stock: 2.0 * ORB_range_15[i]; portfolio: exit all if portfolio_pnl > 0.3% of total capital
exit.stop_loss: per stock: ORB_mid[i]; portfolio: exit all if portfolio loss > 0.3% of total capital
exit.trailing_stop: per stock: after 1.0 * ORB_range[i], trail at ORB_high/low; portfolio: trail at 50% of peak portfolio pnl
exit.time_stop: exit individual stocks if held > 240 mins; exit all by 15:10
exit.signal_exit: if portfolio beta > 1.5 or < -1.5 (too directional), reduce to 3 positions

risk.position_sizing: equal weight: capital_per_stock = total_capital / num_stocks; risk per stock = 0.2%

filters.volume_filter: each stock breakout bar volume > 1.2x 20-bar SMA
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY ORB direction should match majority of stock ORB directions
filters.spread_filter: bid-ask < 0.05% on all stocks at entry
filters.event_filter: exclude stocks with earnings today from the portfolio
other_filters: max 2 stocks from same sector (diversification); portfolio_correlation check is critical

edge.edge_decay_risk: low-moderate — portfolio ORB requires infrastructure to monitor 50 stocks simultaneously

weaknesses: Managing 5-8 simultaneous positions is operationally complex; monitoring, adjusting stops, and exiting all positions requires significant attention and infrastructure
The diversification benefit assumes low correlation between portfolio stocks; on macro-driven days (RBI decision, global event), all stocks correlate to 1.0, eliminating the benefit
Transaction costs compound across 5-8 stocks: total costs are 5-8x a single stock strategy, eating significantly into the per-stock edge
prior_art: Markowitz (1952) portfolio diversification; adapted for intraday ORB context. Similar to Khandani & Lo (2007) on quant portfolio approaches.
notes: Edge math: 0.70 * 18bps - 0.30 * 20bps = 12.6 - 6.0 = 6.6bps gross per stock. Costs ~9bps RT per stock. Net negative per stock! Portfolio edge comes from diversification smoothing: with 6 stocks, the portfolio variance is ~1/3 of single stock. The 25bps daily estimate assumes the portfolio profit distribution is right-skewed (occasional 50+ bps days drive the average).
